events.label: birth
events.text: Born in The Hague to scientist Frederik Ruysch and Maria Post.

evidence.quote: Rachel Ruysch was born on 3 June 1664 in The Hague

events.text: Apprenticed to flower painter Willem van Aelst in Amsterdam at age fifteen.

evidence.quote: In 1679 , at age fifteen , Ruysch was apprenticed to Willem van Aelst

events.text: Began producing and selling independently signed paintings.

evidence.quote: By the time Ruysch was eighteen she was producing and selling independently signed works

events.text: Studies with van Aelst ended at his death.

evidence.quote: Ruysch studied with van Aelst until his death in 1683

events.text: Married Amsterdam portrait painter Juriaen Pool.

evidence.quote: In 1693 she married the Amsterdam portrait painter Juriaen Pool

events.text: Moved with her family to The Hague.

evidence.quote: By 1699 she and her family had moved to The Hague

events.text: Offered membership in the Confrerie Pictura as its first female member.

evidence.quote: By 1699 she and her family had moved to The Hague , where she was offered membership in the Confrerie Pictura

events.text: She and her husband became members of The Hague Painters Guild.

evidence.quote: In 1701 she and her husband became members of The Hague Painters Guild

events.text: Invited to work in Düsseldorf as court painter to Johann Wilhelm, Elector Palatine.

evidence.quote: In 1708 , Ruysch was invited to work for the court in Düsseldorf
She continued working for him and his wife from 1708 until the princes death in 1716

events.text: Court painter service to Johann Wilhelm ended at the prince's death.

evidence.quote: She continued working for him and his wife from 1708 until the princes death in 1716
Ruysch died in Amsterdam on 12 October 1750

events.label: honour
events.text: Included in the Rijksmuseum Gallery of Honor as one of the first women.

evidence.quote: In March of 2021 Leysters work was added to the Gallery of Honor at the Rijksmuseum

undated_mentions: Taught her father and sister Anna Ruysch to paint
Early career: forest floor pictures with small animals, reptiles and fungi
Later adopted flower painting as her main concern
Early signed works in the 1680s influenced by Otto Marseus van Schrieck
